title: Disable Indexes
description: Learn how to disable indexes on a table using the ALTER INDEX statement.

data.text: To disable an index, you use the ALTER INDEX statement with the DISABLE keyword. Disabling an index makes it ineffective for query optimization.

data.title: Disable a single index
data.content: Disables a specific index on a table.

data.title: Disable all indexes on a table
data.content: Disables all indexes on the specified table.
data.code:
ALTER INDEX ALL ON table_name
DISABLE;

items: The query optimizer will not consider the disabled index for query plans.
If you disable a clustered index, you cannot access the table data using SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE until the index is rebuilt or dropped.
SQL Server keeps the index definition in metadata and statistics for nonclustered indexes.

data.text: Disabling a non-clustered index frees its pages and removes it from the optimizer's choices, but the metadata remains so it can be rebuilt. Disabling a clustered index is far more drastic: the table cannot be queried at all until it is rebuilt, because the data lives inside the clustered index.

data.title: Disable, observe, rebuild
data.content: The `is_disabled` flag in `sys.indexes` is how you find indexes left disabled after a failed bulk load.

data.title: Never leave indexes disabled
data.text: A disabled index still appears in tooling, so it is easy to forget. Queries silently fall back to a scan, and the missing index can go unnoticed for months. If you disable indexes for a bulk load, put the rebuild in the same script or in the ETL job's finally block.

data.title: Disable Index Key Points
points: Use ALTER INDEX ... DISABLE to make an index ineffective.
Disabling a clustered index blocks all data access to the table.
Disabling indexes is useful during bulk data loads to avoid index maintenance overhead.
You must rebuild or drop a disabled index to re-enable it.
